summary.text: 菜 is a phonosemantic character for edible plants: 艸 marks the plant category, while 采 supplies a sound cue. It is also used for prepared food or dishes, though the path between these senses is unclear.

formation.text: Phonosemantic: 艸 contributes the plant category and 采 supplies the sound. The character is defined as edible vegetation. A separate proposal derives the word from 采, “gather, pluck,” plus a nominal suffix; that word-history proposal is distinct from the graphic analysis.

components.text: 艹 is the conventional side form of 艸 here. It contributes the plant category, rather than depicting a plant within a scene.
采 supplies the sound in 菜. In its own graphic history, 采 depicts a hand picking from a tree or fruit; that picture is not the referent of 菜.

sound.text: In Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese reconstruction, 菜 *sʰɯːs and 采 *sʰɯːʔ share an onset and rhyme; 菜 has an added departing-tone suffix. Modern Mandarin cài and cǎi retain a related initial and rhyme but differ in tone.

history.text: The curated seal-script-style image illustrates the 艸-plus-采 analysis, but it is a modern redraw in the Shuowen tradition, not an ancient specimen. The consulted inventory also reports bronze forms and a slip-text example; the earliest secure attestation of the full graph remains unclear, and no secure oracle-bone form of 菜 is established here.

Qin slips are reported to spell the vegetable word with 采 in 采羹, and Han examples also use 采 for 菜. This is an earlier spelling practice, not evidence that 菜 originated from 采. Some proposed early bronze and Chu examples containing a 采-like element have disputed readings.

uncertainties.text: The proposal that 菜 derives from 采, “gather, pluck,” plus a nominal suffix is a word-history analysis, not a conclusion established by the character’s 艸-plus-采 structure.

The supplied accounts support vegetable and prepared-food senses but do not establish a comprehensive dated Chinese chronology connecting them. Japanese examples date particular uses, not the origin of the character or the native reading な.

senses.text: The Shuowen definition identifies 菜 as edible vegetation. Qin slips reportedly spell the vegetable word with 采; this supports the word’s use but does not date the first appearance of the full graph 菜.

senses.period: Qin-period example; later Chinese use; Japanese example dated approximately 1120
senses.text: 菜 is used for prepared food or a dish. Qin-period slips reportedly spell the vegetable word with 采, and later Chinese evidence records collective uses for dishes; Japanese sources separately cite a side-dish use around 1120. The evidence does not establish a sequence from vegetables to dishes.
Modern glosses include vegetables, dishes, and food. The supplied definitions do not establish that every gloss is a distinct, chronologically ordered sense.

developments.text: Both senses are attested, but when or how the prepared-food sense developed from edible vegetation is unclear.

limitations.text: The earliest secure attestation of the full graph 菜 and a comprehensive dated Chinese sense history remain unresolved in the consulted material.

overview.text: 菜 names edible plants and vegetables. 艹 marks the plant category, while 采 provides a sound cue; the character is also used for dishes or prepared food.

components.text: 艹 marks the plant category. It is the side form of 艸 in this character.
采 supplies the sound cue. Its hand-and-tree picture belongs to its own graphic history.
